absent: Full definitions, sizes and locking rules for audit context, name, auxiliary and tree structures beyond observed field uses.
Behavior of log start, format, end and helpers for paths, strings, hex, capabilities, keys, task info and object context.
Behavior of syscall, operation and inode filters including state transitions and filter key selection.
Behavior of context reset, detach, free and name release including embedded versus dynamic ownership.
Behavior of watched tree lookup, reference install, table growth, rollback, chunk release and pending removal flushing.
Behavior of special handling and of auxiliary record types other than file capability transitions.
Behavior of process identity logging, daemon detection, architecture query and command line capture plus trimming.
Behavior of parent length computation, name comparison, filesystem type comparison and on-disk capability retrieval.
Behavior of audit panic, warning and fatal trap paths and of configuration change generation.
Concurrency and lifetime rules for per-task state across entry, exit, teardown and nested operation handling.
Numeric values and wire encodings of record identifiers, states, types, flags and field spellings.
Ownership and lifetime of working directory, security properties and message queue attributes held in context.

findings.text: Provides a task teardown routine that releases audit state when a task ends. It first flushes any watched filesystem trees, then for the current task with active state it refreshes filtering and emits a pending event before detaching and freeing the per-task state.

Provides syscall boundary hooks. The entry hook captures call identity plus leading arguments and marks the current context as a syscall event with a timestamp. The exit hook normalizes the result, reapplies filters and emits the complete event when recording is required, then clears the context.

Provides asynchronous operation boundary hooks. The entry hook records the operation code and initializes a dedicated event unless already inside a syscall event. The exit hook normalizes the result and either emits a single operation record when nested or runs full filtering and event emission before clearing state.

Provides filesystem and message queue observation hooks. They attach path names, snapshot inode attributes and capabilities, correlate parent and child directory entries during creation or removal, delegate file observations to inode handling, and stash message queue open parameters with an event marker.

Syscall entry is expected once per traced call on a previously idle context with no pending names, and exit is expected once on a syscall-marked non-placeholder context. Entry is ignored when auditing is off or the task has no state or is disabled; exit clears state in all paths after optional emission.

Uring handling supports nesting inside a syscall event. Entry only stores the operation code when a syscall event is already active. Exit in that nested case filters and emits just the operation record and leaves the outer event for normal syscall exit; otherwise exit performs full event handling and reset.

Filesystem hooks are no-ops when the context is idle. Name attachment creates a new entry for the given path. Inode and child hooks first consult filesystem type filters for exclusion, then reuse or create name entries and snapshot attributes plus tree membership.

A recorded exit produces an ordered family of records: a leading syscall or operation summary, followed by auxiliary data, special handling, descriptor pair and network address when present, per-process identity records, working directory when known, one record per visible name, process title for syscalls, and a final terminator.

Name rendering prefers an explicitly supplied path when available. Otherwise it uses the stored name with length-dependent treatment for full paths, empty relative names and directory prefixes, falling back to the captured working directory or a null placeholder when nothing is available. Identity attributes appear only when an inode was captured, and a name type label plus capabilities always complete the record.

Filtering gates all emission. Disabled state and placeholder contexts skip work. Entry initializes the placeholder marker from rule presence and resets priority when building. Exit and teardown reapply syscall or operation filters plus inode filters and emit only when the resulting state requests recording.

Result normalization maps a range of restart-related negative codes to an interrupted code, except for one ioctl-related code that is preserved. All other codes pass through unchanged. A separate validity marker records success versus failure, and teardown starts from an invalid marker with zero code.

Name bookkeeping keeps a count consistent with list membership. Allocation reuses a small embedded pool until a fixed bound and then uses dynamic allocation with a flag indicating ownership for later release. The first allocation also captures the process working directory when not already held.

Parent and child correlation reuses existing entries when inode and device or name text plus type compatibility match. Otherwise it creates anonymous parent or child entries, with a new child reusing its parent directory name reference. Child handling snapshots the child inode when present or marks the inode as unset.

Tree and filter scans rely on read-side critical sections. Single-inode and ancestry walks look up tree membership under protection, and filesystem type exclusion scans traverse the filter list under protection. The ancestry walk additionally samples a rename sequence number and retries when a concurrent rename or table growth is detected.

Per-task audit state is accessed as caller-owned current task data in these fragments, with no explicit mutex or spinlock shown around context field updates, name list changes or reset. Correctness appears to depend on boundary hook serialization per task, which the fragments do not define.

The per-task state observed here carries event identity and timing, call or operation identity with arguments, result code plus validity, filter outcome and key, personality and architecture, name count and list with embedded pool, tree references and count with pending removals, auxiliary and process identity chains, descriptor pair, network address, target identity, working directory, cached process title, queue open parameters and dummy plus priority markers.

Name entries observed here link into a per-event list and carry a path reference with reference count, a length marker distinguishing full paths from directory prefixes, inode number plus device and mode plus ownership plus raw device, security properties, a record type, a visibility flag, on-disk capability sets with version, and an ownership flag for dynamic release.

Auxiliary chains observed here include file capability transition records with version plus file and old versus new process capability sets plus root identity, process identity chains with counts plus identifiers plus names, message queue open parameters with flags plus mode plus attributes, and an event type marker.

Context identity moves from idle to either syscall or operation on entry and returns to idle on exit or reset. Teardown also detaches to no state. Nesting is special: operation entry inside a syscall event does not change identity, and nested operation exit emits without resetting, leaving reset to the outer syscall exit.

Name type starts as unknown on allocation. Inode handling promotes it to parent for directory components or to normal for final components, with an optional hidden marker for parents. Child handling promotes unknown entries to the caller-supplied create or delete variant or creates fresh parent and child entries already typed.

Tree reference installation can fail for lack of space. The code warns, marks the event as auditable to force retention, releases any partially acquired reference and rolls back references added during the attempt. Ancestry handling retries after growing the table and only forces retention when growth fails.

Misuse is treated as fatal or exceptional. Entry on a busy context or with pending names warns and raises an audit panic without proceeding. Exit dispatch on an unexpected context identity traps. These paths indicate a lifecycle bug rather than a normal refusal.

Most logging start failures silently skip that record, relying on an internal panic path elsewhere. Two cases set a sticky error flag instead: security object logging and per-process identity logging. The flag causes a final audit panic after the terminator is emitted, so one bad subrecord fails the whole event.

Record and event identifiers observed in these fragments include AUDIT_PATH for name records and AUDIT_PROCTITLE for title records and AUDIT_URINGOP for operation records and AUDIT_SYSCALL for syscall summaries and AUDIT_BPRM_FCAPS for capability transitions and AUDIT_FD_PAIR for descriptor pairs and AUDIT_SOCKADDR for socket addresses and AUDIT_CWD for working directory and AUDIT_EOE for event termination and AUDIT_MQ_OPEN for queue open typing.

Context identities include AUDIT_CTX_UNUSED for idle and AUDIT_CTX_SYSCALL for syscalls and AUDIT_CTX_URING for operations. Build and record gating uses AUDIT_STATE_DISABLED and AUDIT_STATE_BUILD and AUDIT_STATE_RECORD. Result validity uses AUDITSC_INVALID and AUDITSC_SUCCESS and AUDITSC_FAILURE.

Name handling markers include AUDIT_NAME_FULL for full paths and AUDIT_INO_UNSET for missing inodes and AUDIT_NAMES as the embedded pool bound. Record typing uses AUDIT_TYPE_UNKNOWN and AUDIT_TYPE_NORMAL and AUDIT_TYPE_PARENT and AUDIT_TYPE_CHILD_CREATE and AUDIT_TYPE_CHILD_DELETE. Inode flags include AUDIT_INODE_PARENT and AUDIT_INODE_HIDDEN and AUDIT_INODE_NOEVAL. Filesystem filtering uses AUDIT_FILTER_FS with field AUDIT_FSTYPE and action AUDIT_NEVER.

Allocation modes observed include GFP_KERNEL for process context and GFP_ATOMIC for operation logging and GFP_NOFS for name growth. Title capture is bounded by MAX_PROCTITLE_AUDIT_LEN. Personality comparison uses PER_LINUX. Restart normalization references ERESTARTSYS through ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK with EINTR as replacement and ENOIOCTLCMD as exclusion. Capability decoding uses VFS_CAP_FLAGS_EFFECTIVE and VFS_CAP_REVISION_MASK with VFS_CAP_REVISION_SHIFT.
